title.en: EU’s Kallas criticises Putin’s ‘very cynical’ Ukraine ceasefire calls and rejects suggestion of Schröder as mediator – Europe live

summary.en: EU officials, including Estonia's former Prime Minister Kaja Kallas, have dismissed Russian President Vladimir Putin's calls for a ceasefire in Ukraine as "cynical" and rejected the suggestion of former German chancellor Gerhard Schröder as a mediator. Meanwhile, Poland's former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro is...
summary.zh: 欧盟官员，包括爱沙尼亚前总理卡娅·卡拉斯，驳斥了俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京关于乌克兰停火的呼吁是“玩世不恭”的，并拒绝了由德国前总理格哈德·施罗德担任调解人的提议。与此同时，波兰前司法部长兹比格涅夫·齐奥布罗因20多项刑事指控被波兰当局通缉。

body.en:
EU’s foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas earlier was also dismissive of Putin’s “very cynical” calls for a ceasefire “to protect his parade, whereas they were actually still attacking civilians in Ukraine .”

And the former Estonian prime minister, too, was not particularly keen on Schröder as a mediator on Ukraine.

“If we give the right to Russia to appoint a negotiator on our behalf, that would not be very wise.

And second, I think Gerhard Schröder has been the high-level lobbyist for Russian state-owned companies, so it’s clear why Putin wants him to be the person so that actually he would be sitting on both sides of the table.”

Kallas also warned against broader Russian operations in Europe, warning that “clearly, our adversaries are not sleeping; so clearly, they want to increase the influence in Europe.”

“We unfortunately already see this in sports organisations, where, you know, Russians are let to compete like nothing has happened. And there are discussions there. We also saw this Venice Biennale where they are there like nothing has happened. So clearly they are working all the time and we have to be vigilant as well.”
body.zh: 欧盟外交政策负责人和前爱沙尼亚总理驳回了普京关于德国前总理可以协调谈判的建议。与此同时，波兰前司法部长齐比格涅夫·齐奥布罗因涉嫌 20 多项刑事指控而被波兰当局通缉，他于周末移居美国，离开匈牙利，在那里他获得了前维克多·欧尔班政府给予的政治庇护。齐奥布罗是法律与正义党政府中最著名的人物之一，并在其备受争议的司法改革中发挥了核心作用，批评者称这些改革破坏了法治和法院的独立性，导致与欧盟的长期冲突。继续阅读...

title.en: Bosnia's powerful peace envoy quits, with questions over role's future
title.zh: 波斯尼亚强大的和平特使辞职，其角色未来成疑

summary.en: Christian Schmidt, who served as Bosnia's peace envoy since 2021, has resigned from his position. His departure comes amid questions about the future of the role, particularly after he reportedly lost the support of the United States.
summary.zh: 自2021年起担任波斯尼亚和平特使的克里斯蒂安·施密特已辞去职务。他的离职引发了人们对该角色未来的疑问，尤其是在他据称失去了美国的支持之后。

body.en:
The most powerful figure in Bosnia and Herzegovina has confirmed that he is stepping down.

Christian Schmidt has served as international high representative since 2021, the second-longest tenure of any high representative. His time in the post was filled with conflict and controversy.

His office said that Schmidt "has taken the personal decision to conclude his service to the implementation of peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina".

His appointment was never approved by Russia and now it seems he has also lost the support of the US, making his position untenable. A broader conundrum is whether the Office of the High Representative itself has a future and, if not, where that would leave Bosnia.

The role dates back to the 1995 Dayton Peace Agreement which ended the country's ruinous ethnic conflict.

The UN-appointed high representative is supposed to ensure that the agreement is followed and has wide-ranging powers to keep the country's ever-fractious ethno-political leaders in line.

During his stint as high representative, Paddy Ashdown memorably wielded these so-called "Bonn Powers" sacking 60 Bosnian-Serb officials in one day in 2004 for refusing to cooperate with the Hague Tribunal.

Ashdown duly received the not entirely flattering nickname of "Viceroy of Bosnia".

Subsequent holders of the office were far more low key. Bosnia and Herzegovina's international supporters focused on the country's leaders dealing with their affairs on their own.

The failure of that approach was reflected by Schmidt's more activist role following his appointment.

He repeatedly used the Bonn Powers to block separatist legislation promoted by the Bosnian-Serb leader, Milorad Dodik, who ignored these blocks. This struggle led to Dodik receiving a one-year prison sentence and six-year ban on holding public office.

But it appears that Dodik will be the long-term winner. His expensive deployment of Washington lobbyists paid off when the US lifted its long-term sanctions on him.

Cynics have noted Dodik's subsequent support for the award of a major gas pipeline project to a hitherto obscure US company with links to the Trump family. In contrast, Schmidt's reservations about the project appear to have cost him Washington's support.

Schmidt says he will remain in office until a successor is selected. But Russia has repeatedly backed up Dodik's calls for closure of the Office of the High Representative.

If the US takes a similar stance, Bosnia could lose the only figure who can act as a safeguard against the separatist ambitions of ethno-nationalist leaders.
body.zh: 波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那最有权势的人物已确认辞职。 克里斯蒂安·施密特自 2021 年起担任国际高级代表，是所有高级代表中任期第二长的。他任职期间充满了冲突和争议。 他的办公室表示，施密特“已做出个人决定，结束他对实现波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那和平的服务”。 他的任命从未得到俄罗斯的批准，现在看来他也失去了美国的支持，让他的地位站不住脚。一个更广泛的难题是高级代表办公室本身是否有未来，如果没有，波斯尼亚将走向何方。 这一角色可以追溯到 1995 年《代顿和平协议》，该协议结束了该国毁灭性的种族冲突。 联合国任命的高级代表应该确保协议得到遵守，并拥有广泛的权力来让该国脾气暴躁的民族政治领导人保持一致。 2004 年，在担任高级代表期间，帕迪·阿什当 (Paddy Ashdown) 令人难忘地运用了这些所谓的“波恩权力”，一天之内解雇了 60 名拒绝与海牙法庭合作的波斯尼亚塞族官员。 阿什当正式获得了“波斯尼亚总督”这个不太讨人喜欢的绰号。 随后担任该职位的人则低调得多。波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那的国际支持者关注的是该国领导人自行处理自己的事务。 施密特在上任后扮演的更加激进的角色反映了这种方法的失败。 他多次利用波恩权力来阻止波斯尼亚-塞族领导人米洛拉德·多迪克推动的分离主义立法，但多迪克却无视这些阻止。这场斗争导致多迪克被判入狱一年，并禁止担任公职六年。 但看来多迪克将成为长期赢家。当美国解除对他的长期制裁时，他在华盛顿游说者的昂贵部署得到了回报。 愤世嫉俗者注意到，多迪克随后支持将一个大型天然气管道项目授予一家迄今为止默默无闻、与特朗普家族有联系的美国公司。相比之下，施密特对该项目的保留似乎让他失去了华盛顿的支持。 施密特表示，在选出继任者之前，他将继续留任。但俄罗斯一再支持多迪克关闭高级代表办公室的呼吁。 如果美国采取类似的立场，波斯尼亚可能会失去唯一能够抵御民族主义领导人分离主义野心的人物。

reflection.en: The departure of a key peace envoy raises questions about the future direction and stability of a region. When leadership or a clear vision for peace is absent, societies can struggle to maintain order and progress. This reminds us of the importance of sustained guidance and commitment to foster lasting peace.
reflection.zh: 一位关键和平特使的离职，引发了人们对一个地区未来方向和稳定性的疑问。当和平的领导力或清晰愿景缺失时，社会可能难以维持秩序和进步。这提醒我们，持续的指导和承诺对于促进持久和平至关重要。

verse.textEn: Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint; but blessed is the one who heeds wisdom's instruction.
verse.textZh: 没有异象，民就放肆；惟遵守律法的，便为有福。

title.en: US and French nationals test positive for hantavirus after leaving ship
title.zh: 美法公民下船后汉坦病毒检测呈阳性

summary.en: Two individuals, an American and a French national, have tested positive for hantavirus after disembarking from a ship. The American is now in Nebraska, and the French woman is in isolation in Paris.
summary.zh: 两名分别来自美国和法国的公民在下船后被检测出汉坦病毒呈阳性。这名美国公民已抵达内布拉斯加州，而法国女性正在巴黎进行隔离。

body.en:
An American and a French national who have returned to their home countries having left a cruise ship hit by a deadly outbreak of hantavirus have tested positive, authorities say.

In total seven cases of hantavirus linked to the MV Hondius have been confirmed, with two other cases suspected, the World Health Organization (WHO) said on Monday.

The US health department said a second American national on the repatriation flight had also shown mild symptoms, adding that both passengers had travelled back in "biocontainment units out of an abundance of caution".

French Health Minister Stéphanie Rist said a woman was isolating in Paris and her health was deteriorating, with 22 contacts traced.

Three passengers have died after travelling on the ship, two of whom were confirmed to have had the virus.

The WHO said the person who is believed to have been the first to be infected in the outbreak died before he could be tested.

Two other British nationals with confirmed cases are currently being treated in the Netherlands and South Africa.

Hantaviruses are usually carried by rodents , but human transmission of the Andes strain - which the World Health Organization (WHO) believes was contracted by some of the Dutch ship's passengers while in South America - is possible.

Symptoms can include fever, extreme fatigue, muscle aches, stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhoea and shortness of breath.

More than 90 passengers of the MV Hondius ship, currently docked in Spain's Canary Islands, are being repatriated.

In its latest update from Tenerife on Monday, Spanish officials said 54 passengers and crew were still on board the ship. Spanish Health Minister Mónica García said six of those were passengers: four Australians, one Briton and one New Zealander.

Some 22 people would disembark the ship to fly to the Netherlands on Monday, she said - including the Australians who had been expected to be flown home directly but whose plane could not be guaranteed to arrive on time.

The MV Hondius was then expected to leave for the Netherlands later on Monday, she said.

Four Canadian passengers, meanwhile, have landed in Victoria, British Columbia, on Sunday evening after taking a chartered flight from Tenerife to Bagotville, Quebec. Authorities said they would be self-isolating and monitored for at least three weeks.

In its statement early on Monday, the US Department of Health and Human Services said all 17 US citizens on Sunday's flight would undergo "clinical assessment" at a medical facility in Nebraska. A British national living in the US was also repatriated alongside them.

Seven other US passengers had already returned home and were being monitored in their home states.

body.zh: 当局称，一名美国人和一名法国人在离开一艘遭受致命汉坦病毒爆发的游轮后返回自己的祖国，他们的检测结果呈阳性。 美国卫生部门表示，撤侨航班上的另一名美国公民也出现了轻微症状，并补充说，两名乘客都是“出于高度谨慎”而乘坐生物隔离舱返回的。 法国卫生部长斯蒂芬妮·里斯特表示，一名妇女在巴黎接受隔离，她的健康状况正在恶化，已追踪到 22 名接触病例。 目前停靠在西班牙加那利群岛的 MV Hondius 轮船上的 90 多名乘客正在被遣返。 三名乘客——一对荷兰夫妇和一名德国妇女——在船上旅行后死亡。其中两人被确认感染了病毒。 汉坦病毒通常由啮齿类动物携带，但安第斯病毒株也可能在人类中传播——世界卫生组织 (WHO) 认为这种病毒是由荷兰游轮上的一些乘客在南美期间感染的。 症状包括发烧、极度疲劳、肌肉酸痛、胃痛、呕吐、腹泻和呼吸急促。 美国卫生与公众服务部在周一早些时候的声明中表示，该航班上的所有 17 名美国公民将在内布拉斯加州的一家医疗机构“接受临床评估”。 另外七名美国乘客已经返回，并正在其家乡接受监测。 一名居住在美国的英国国民与 17 名美国乘客一起撤离。 在美国确诊病例之前，世卫组织总干事谭德塞警告说，美国决定不遵循该组织针对汉坦病毒爆发的指导方针“可能存在风险”。 但美国疾病控制中心（CDC）代理主任杰伊·巴塔查里亚（Jay Bhattacharya）博士表示，他不想引起公众恐慌，坚称人际传播很少见，不应像新冠病毒一样对待。 周日，游轮乘客在特内里费岛格兰迪拉德阿沃纳港下船时，被拍到身穿蓝色长袍，戴着蓬松的帽子，戴着医用口罩。 乘客乘坐包机从特内里费岛飞往曼彻斯特机场，并被送往默西塞德郡威勒尔的阿罗公园医院隔离72小时。他们都没有报告症状。 另外两名确诊病例的英国国民目前正在荷兰和南非接受治疗。 在西班牙，飞往马德里的 14 名西班牙人目前在一家军医院面临强制隔离。另外两架疏散航班定于周一下午进行。 周日，另一架载有 26 名乘客和机组人员（其中包括 8 名荷兰公民）的航班抵达荷兰。 六名乘客正在返回澳大利亚，另一名乘客...

reflection.en: News of individuals testing positive for a virus reminds us of our shared human vulnerability to illness. In such moments, we are called to remember those who are sick and isolated, offering prayers for their healing and recovery. This situation underscores the importance of care and compassion for all who face health challenges.
reflection.zh: 有人病毒检测呈阳性的消息提醒我们，人类在疾病面前的共同脆弱性。在这样的时刻，我们被呼召去记念那些生病和被隔离的人，为他们的康复和痊愈献上祷告。这种情况强调了对所有面临健康挑战的人给予关怀和同情的重要性。

verse.textEn: Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.
verse.textZh: 你们中间有病了的呢，他就该请教会的长老来；他们可以奉主的名用油抹他，为他祷告。

title.en: Middle East crisis live: Trump rejects Iran response to US peace proposal as Tehran warns of new attacks
title.zh: 中东危机：特朗普拒绝伊朗对美国和平提议的回应，德黑兰警告将发动新袭击

summary.en: The US president has rejected Iran's response to a peace proposal, calling it “totally unacceptable.” Tehran, in turn, has warned of retaliation against any new US strikes or foreign warships in the Strait of Hormuz, as a ceasefire in the region frays.
summary.zh: 美国总统已拒绝伊朗对和平提议的回应，称其“完全不可接受”。德黑兰则警告称，如果美国再次发动袭击或有外国军舰进入霍尔木兹海峡，伊朗将进行报复，目前该地区的停火协议正在瓦解。

body.en: US president calls Iranian response ‘totally unacceptable’ while Tehran says it will retaliate against any new US strikes or foreign warships in strait of Hormuz Trump calls Iran’s response to peace plan ‘totally unacceptable’ as ceasefire frays Turkey’s foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, will visit Qatar later today for talks on the war, its impact on the region and efforts to ensure navigational safety in the strait of Hormuz is resumed, a Turkish diplomatic source told the Reuters news agency. Turkey, which neighbours Iran, has been in close contact with the US, Iran and mediator Pakistan since the start of the conflict. It condemnded the US and Israel for launching the war, widely seen to have been done illegally, but also criticised Iran’s counter strikes on Gulf states. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The rejection of a peace proposal and subsequent threats of retaliation highlight the persistent challenge of breaking cycles of conflict. In such moments, it is easy for nations to be overcome by the temptation to respond to perceived evil with further aggression. Yet, the call remains to seek ways to overcome evil with good, even when peace seems distant.
reflection.zh: 和平提议被拒绝以及随之而来的报复威胁，凸显了打破冲突循环的持续挑战。在这样的时刻，国家很容易被诱惑，以进一步的侵略来回应所认为的邪恶。然而，即使和平看似遥远，我们仍被呼召寻求以善胜恶的途径。

verse.textEn: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
verse.textZh: 你不可为恶所胜，反要以善胜恶。

This comes as many voters express a feeling that the country is not working for them.

She is a working-class Yorkshire woman, she says. She knows that the opportunities she has enjoyed would not be there if if had not been for the achievements of Labour government. She says Labour is one of the best vehicles for changing the lives of working people that this county has ever known. Continue reading...

reflection.en: In times when people feel their nation lacks direction, leaders often step forward to articulate a new vision. Proverbs 29:18 reminds us that without a clear vision, people can become disoriented and lose their way. This highlights the profound responsibility of leadership to offer hope and a path forward, addressing the deep-seated concerns of the populace.
reflection.zh: 当人们感到国家缺乏方向时，领袖们常会站出来阐明新的愿景。箴言29:18提醒我们，没有清晰的异象，百姓就会放纵，失去方向。这突显了领导者提供希望和前进道路的深远责任，以回应民众深层的担忧。

verse.textEn: Where there is no revelation, people cast off restraint; but blessed is the one who heeds wisdom's instruction.
verse.textZh: 没有异象，民就放肆；惟遵守律法的，便为有福。

title.en: What will happen to Iran's nuclear material?
title.zh: 伊朗的核材料将会怎样？

summary.en: Iran is believed to have over 440 kilos (970 pounds) of enriched uranium, which could be turned into weapons-grade nuclear material. Despite Trump's pledge to get the "nuclear dust," Tehran has kept it out of US reach.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Iran is believed to have over 440 kilos (970 pounds) of enriched uranium, which could be turned into weapons-grade nuclear material. Despite Trump's pledge to get the "nuclear dust," Tehran has kept it out of US reach.

Iran's nuclear program has been a source of strife for decades, with two generations of Iranians now associating words like as yellowcake, centrifuges, and enrichment with crisis, instability, and war. The regime's insistence on uranium enrichment has exposed the country to heavy sanctions, and some estimates have put the direct economic damage at around $3.5 trillion (€3 trillion).

Throughout the recent military conflicts and fragile ceasefires between Tehran and Washington, the program has once again taken center stage. The US seems particularly focused on Iran's nuclear stockpile — Tehran is believed to have over 440 kilos (970 pounds) of uranium already enriched to 60%, far above what is necessary for civilian purposes. Theoretically, this material could be enriched further to reach 90% in a relatively short time , making it suitable for use in nuclear weapons.

US President Donald Trump often refers to the material as "nuclear dust" in reference to the June 2025 bombing which he claims "obliterated" Iran's nuclear program. Trump has repeatedly stated that the US will take possession of it, but also provided contradictory statements on how this will be done, including claims that the US will be "going in, with Iran, with lots of excavators" to dig it out from under the rubble, presumably after a peace accord is reached. In April, Trump said Iran had agreed to hand over its stockpile, while last week he seemed to indicate that the US will "take a hit" because "we have to make a journey down to Iran to take the nuclear weapon."

Iran has yet to confirm any deal involving the uranium stockpile. Talking to US broadcaster CBS In March, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the material remains under the rubble following last year's attack and that Iran had "no program" and "no plan" to recover the material.

However, Araghchi was also careful not to exclude the possibility of diluting the highly enriched uranium as part of a future deal with the US .

Recent media reports also indicated that Iran was ready to dilute part of its stockpile while transferring the rest to a third country. This weekend, Russian President Vladimir Putin said his country was ready store Iran's enriched uranium.

However, it is still unclear where the material is located and what technical challenges needed to be overcome in order to access it.

Iran's top three nuclear facilities — Isfahan, Fordow and Natanz — all suffered heavy damage during last year's Operation "Midnight Hammer."

body.zh: 据信伊朗拥有超过 440 公斤（970 磅）的浓缩铀，可以转化为武器级核材料。尽管特朗普承诺获得“核尘埃”，但德黑兰却将其置于美国的控制范围之外。 几十年来，伊朗的核计划一直是冲突的根源，两代伊朗人现在将“黄饼”、“离心机”和“浓缩”等词与危机、不稳定和战争联系在一起。该政权坚持进行铀浓缩活动，导致该国面临严厉制裁，一些估计直接经济损失约为 3.5 万亿美元（3 万亿欧元）。 在德黑兰和华盛顿之间最近的军事冲突和脆弱的停火中，该计划再次成为焦点。美国似乎特别关注伊朗的核储备——据信德黑兰拥有超过 440 公斤（970 磅）的铀，浓​​缩度已达到 60%，远远高于民用目的所需的量。理论上，这种材料可以在相对较短的时间内进一步浓缩至 90%，使其适合用于核武器。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在提到 2025 年 6 月的爆炸事件时经常将这种材料称为“核尘埃”，他声称那次爆炸“摧毁了”伊朗的核计划。特朗普一再表示美国将拥有它，但也就如何做到这一点提供了相互矛盾的声明，包括声称美国将“与伊朗一起，用大量挖掘机”将其从废墟下挖掘出来，大概是在达成和平协议之后。今年四月，特朗普表示伊朗已同意交出其库存，而上周他似乎表示美国将“受到打击”，因为“我们必须前往伊朗获取核武器”。 伊朗尚未确认任何涉及铀库存的交易。今年三月，伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇在接受美国广播公司哥伦比亚广播公司采访时表示，去年袭击后这些材料仍然埋在废墟下，伊朗“没有计划”也“没有计划”回收这些材料。 然而，阿拉格奇也小心翼翼地不排除稀释高浓缩铀作为未来与美国协议的一部分的可能性。 最近的媒体报道还表明，伊朗准备稀释部分库存，同时将其余库存转移到第三国。本周末，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京表示，俄罗斯已准备好储存伊朗的浓缩铀。 然而，目前尚不清楚这些材料位于何处，以及需要克服哪些技术挑战才能获取这些材料。 伊朗三大核设施——伊斯法罕、福尔多和纳坦兹——在去年的“午夜之锤”行动中均遭受严重破坏。 国际原子能机构总干事拉斐尔·格罗西...

summary.en: High-tech missions are tracking critically low snowpack levels across the mountains of the US west, raising alarm among experts. The data reveals a pristine white appearance from above belies significant environmental degradation.

Continue reading...

Members of the British Army have parachuted onto the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha to help a British national with suspected hantavirus.

Two paratroopers jumped in tandem with an intensive care nurse and a specialist doctor. Medical supplies were also delivered.

The patient left MV Hondius, the cruise ship hit by a deadly outbreak of the virus, in mid-April at Britain's most remote inhabited overseas territory, where he lives.

Captain George Lacey, who jumped with the Pathfinders Platoon, based at Colchester Garrison, said high winds made it the mission "a particularly tricky one".

He said the team would be on the island for a few days awaiting recovery, because "sadly, you can't parachute back off the island".

Local teacher Gillian Welch, who piloted a cart, says it is a "brilliant event".

body.zh: 英国陆军成员跳伞到偏远的大西洋岛屿特里斯坦达库尼亚岛，以帮助一名疑似感染汉坦病毒的英国国民。 两名伞兵与一名重症监护护士和一名专科医生一起跳伞。医疗用品也已送达。 4月中旬，这名患者在他所居住的英国最偏远的海外有人居住的地区离开了遭受致命病毒爆发的MV Hondius游轮。 乔治·莱西上尉是驻扎在科尔切斯特驻军的探路者排的一员，他表示，强风使得这次任务“特别棘手”。 他说，团队将在岛上待几天等待恢复，因为“遗憾的是，你无法从岛上跳伞回来”。 驾驶手推车的当地教师吉莉安·韦尔奇 (Gillian Welch) 表示，这是一次“精彩的活动”。 一辆疑似失窃的汽车被以超过限制速度两倍的速度跟踪，随后两名男子试图逃跑。 自行车手和观众聚集在银行假日的阳光下，观看一年一度的绍森德赛。 据报道，维多利亚·菲格雷多·巴雷托 (Vitoria Figueiredo Barreto) 于 3 月 4 日拜访朋友后失踪。 陪审团观看了两名男子被指控在埃平贝尔酒店外实施暴力骚乱的录像。 警方称，该房产已变成“规模庞大且组织良好的大麻工厂”。 该男子否认在驾驶时使用智能手机的导航应用程序，直到检察官出示录像。 在花费 7,000 英镑警告司机注意鸭子后，一名居民对这个半开玩笑的标志表示欢迎。 警方称，碰撞前该车的行驶速度超过 100 英里/小时（160 公里/小时）。 视频显示，一辆汽车撞上几辆停放的车辆和一座建筑物，然后翻倒。 视频显示，库马约尔的一个山谷发生雪崩后，包括儿童在内的一排人被雪覆盖。 送货司机按照 GPS 指令操作后，货车被困在潮汐泥滩上。 2024 年 2 月，阿什利·沃伦 (Ashley Warren) 抵达滨海克拉克顿时被警方拘留。 消防人员和一名农民使用伸缩臂叉装机将 18 岁的小马艺伎从洞里救了出来。 陪审员们看到警察在埃塞克斯郡杰威克的一处房产中使用泰瑟枪制止狗的瞬间。 杰米·奥利弗 (Jamie Oliver) 表示，他“很可能正在考虑”出现在 BBC 名人版节目中。 司机未能停车报警，警方怀疑他的车牌被克隆，汽车被盗。 三人航海队在不到 43 天的时间里从西班牙划行了 3,000 英里（4,828 公里）到达安提瓜岛。 杰里米·希思 (Jeremy Heath) 谋杀一名驾驶四驱车的男子两天后被武装警察拘留。

title.en: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer 'not walking away' after local election mauling
title.zh: 英国首相凯尔·斯塔默在地方选举遭受重创后“没有走开”

summary.en: Keir Starmer has said he takes "responsibility" for Labour's poor election performance, but also for putting matters right again. "I know I have my doubters and I know I need to prove them wrong, and I will," he said.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 基尔·斯塔默表示，他对工党糟糕的选举表现负有“责任”，但也对纠正问题负有责任。 “我知道有人怀疑我，我知道我需要证明他们是错的，我会的，”他说。 英国首相基尔·斯塔默周一在伦敦语气好斗，表示在上周全国大选惨败后，他无意辞职。 这是在公众压力下做出的，甚至党内也有一些声音敦促他重新考虑自己的立场。 “上周的选举结果很艰难。非常艰难，”斯塔默说。 “这很痛，也应该很痛。我明白。我感觉到了。我承担责任。但这不仅仅是对结果负责。” 他表示，他还有责任解释英国政府计划如何做得更好，并称该国正面临“危险的时期和危险的对手”。 斯塔默说：“如果我们做不好这一点，我们将走上一条非常黑暗的道路。” “我有责任不走开，不让我们的国家陷入混乱，就像保守党一次又一次所做的那样。混乱将对这个国家造成持久的损害。” 他说他知道有人怀疑他，需要证明他们是错的，并表示他会这样做。 斯塔默发表讲话的几天前，他的工党在英国市政选举以及苏格兰和威尔士的国家议会选举中遭受重创，这两个国家都是工党历史上的中心地带。 工党失去了英格兰各地 1,400 多个议会席位，影响力同时流向了民粹主义右翼的改革英国和民粹主义左翼的绿党。 在威尔士参议院，该党的得票率从36.2%、30个席位下降至11.1%、9个席位，从第一大党跌至远远落后于威尔士民族主义者格莱德·西姆鲁党和改革英国党的第三位。 在北方，工党看到苏格兰民族党重新确立了其在荷里路德议院的主导地位，尽管近年来它自己也遇到了重大困难。改革党在苏格兰赢得了与工党一样多的席位； 绿党、保守党和自由民主党紧随其后。 自2024年大选获胜以来，各种政策大转变、沟通问题以及彼得·曼德尔森被任命为美国大使的旷日持久的丑闻让工党面临压力。 周末，资历相对较低的国会议员、前低级别部长凯瑟琳·韦斯特 (Catherine West) 敦促她的同事在周一之前向斯塔默的领导层发起挑战。韦斯特说，如果他们不这样做，她会考虑自己做。 工党备受瞩目的前副党魁安吉拉·雷纳(Angela Rayner)并没有违背斯塔默的信仰，但周日晚上，她确实发布了一份长长的购物清单，列出了她认为工党取得的成就……

title.en: Ailing Iranian Nobel laureate given bail and hospital transfer
title.zh: 患病伊朗诺贝尔奖得主获准保释并转院

summary.en: Iranian authorities have granted human rights activist and Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi bail, allowing her transfer to a hospital due to serious health concerns while in prison.
summary.zh: 伊朗当局已批准人权活动家、诺贝尔奖得主纳尔吉斯·穆罕默迪保释，允许她因狱中健康状况严重而转院治疗。

body.en:
Iranian Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi has been transferred from jail to a Tehran hospital amid concern over her deteriorating health.

Iranian authorities granted the human rights activist "a sentence suspension on heavy bail", a foundation run by her family said on Sunday.

Her brother, Hamidreza, told the BBC that he was relieved she would now receive adequate treatment from her own medical team. But he cautioned that the seriousness of her condition was not yet clear.

Last week, Mohammadi's family and supporters warned she could die in prison after suffering two suspected heart attacks earlier this year.

The 54-year-old, who is vice-president of the Defenders of Human Rights Center in Iran, was awarded the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize for her activism against female oppression in Iran and promoting human rights.

After pleas from her family for her to be transferred from prison, Mohammadi was "now at Tehran Pars Hospital to be treated by her own medical team", ​the Narges Mohammadi Foundation said in a statement on Sunday evening.

She had spent 10 days at a hospital in Zanjan, about 265km (165 miles) north-west of the capital, where she was serving her sentence.

"Narges Mohammadi's life hangs in the balance," her Paris-based husband, Taghi Rahmani, said in a statement.

"While she is currently hospitalised following a catastrophic health failure, a temporary transfer is not enough. Narges must never be returned to the conditions that broke her health," he added.

Hamidreza Mohammadi, her Oslo-based brother, told the BBC that the bail provided "temporary relief from the certain death that Narges faced in the prison".

"It's very early stages, so we don't have any precise news about what's going on. But we trust the doctors that have treated her before. The only worry that I have is the permanent damage that has been caused during these days in the prison," he said.

"She has been experiencing very serious symptoms that point in the direction of having developed variant angina," he added, referring to a heart condition that happens when a coronary artery supplying blood and oxygen to your heart goes into spasm and suddenly narrows. "It might have some life-long repercussions for her health."

The activist is believed to have lost about 20kg (three stone) while in prison, and has difficulty speaking and is barely recognisable, according to her lawyer Chirinne Ardakani, who posted a photo of her sitting up in a hospital bed .

Mohammadi has spent more than a decade of her life in prison. In 2021, she began serving a 13-year sentence on charges of committing "propaganda activity against the state" and "collusion against state security", which she denied.

In December 2024, she was given a temporary release from Tehran's notorious Evin prison...
body.zh: 由于担心健康状况恶化，伊朗诺贝尔和平奖获得者纳尔吉斯·穆罕默迪已从监狱转移到德黑兰一家医院。 她家人经营的一个基金会周日表示，伊朗当局给予这位人权活动家“缓刑并重额保释”。 她的兄弟哈米德雷扎告诉英国广播公司，他很高兴她现在可以从自己的医疗团队那里得到充分的治疗。但他警告说，目前尚不清楚她病情的严重性。 上周，穆罕默迪的家人和支持者警告说，她今年早些时候两次疑似心脏病发作，可能会死在监狱里。 这位 54 岁的伊朗人权捍卫者中心副主席因其反对伊朗女性压迫和促进人权的活动而被授予 2023 年诺贝尔和平奖。 纳尔吉斯·穆罕默迪基金会在周日晚间的一份声明中表示，在家人请求将她从监狱转移出来后，穆罕默迪“现在在德黑兰帕尔斯医院接受她自己的医疗团队的治疗”。 她在首都西北约 265 公里（165 英里）处的赞詹一家医院服刑 10 天。 “纳尔吉斯·穆罕默迪的生命悬而未决，”她在巴黎的丈夫塔吉·拉赫马尼在一份声明中说。 “虽然她目前因灾难性的健康问题而住院，但暂时转移是不够的。纳尔吉斯绝不能回到破坏她健康的状况，”他补充道。 她在奥斯陆的兄弟哈米德雷扎·穆罕默迪 (Hamidreza Mohammadi) 告诉英国广播公司 (BBC)，保释让“纳尔吉斯暂时摆脱了在监狱中面临的死亡威胁”。 “现在还处于早期阶段，所以我们没有任何关于正在发生的事情的确切消息。但我们相信以前治疗过她的医生。我唯一担心的是这些天在监狱里造成的永久性伤害，”他说。 他补充说：“她一直在经历非常严重的症状，这些症状表明她患有变异性心绞痛。”变异性心绞痛指的是向心脏供应血液和氧气的冠状动脉痉挛并突然狭窄时发生的心脏病。 “这可能会对她的健康产生一些终生的影响。” 她的律师 Chirinne Ardakani 发布了一张她坐在医院病床上的照片，据信她在监狱期间体重减轻了约 20 公斤（三英石），并且说话有困难，几乎无法辨认。 穆罕默迪在监狱中度过了十多年的人生。 2021年，她开始服刑13年，罪名是“反国家宣传活动”和“共谋危害国家安全”，但她否认了这一点。 2024 年 12 月，她从德黑兰臭名昭著的埃文监狱暂时获释……

title.en: Portrait looted by Nazis found in home of Dutch SS leader's descendants
title.zh: 在荷兰党卫军领导人后裔家中发现纳粹掠夺的肖像

summary.en: The painting is believed to have been plundered by high-ranking Nazi Hermann Goering during World War Two.

body.en:
A painting stolen from a Jewish art collector by the Nazis during World War Two has been found in the home of descendants of a notorious Dutch SS collaborator, an art detective has said.

Portrait of a Young Girl, by Dutch artist Toon Kelder, is believed to have hung for decades in the home of Hendrik Seyffardt's family, Arthur Brand said.

It had belonged to Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker, who died while fleeing the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands in 1940, leaving behind a collection of more than 1,000 paintings.

The case was brought to Brand's attention by a man who told him he was a descendant of Seyffardt and that he was "disgusted" to learn his family had kept the artwork for years.

Seyffardt was a Dutch general who commanded a Waffen-SS unit of volunteers on the eastern front before he was assassinated by resistance fighters in 1943.

Shortly after learning he was related to the Nazi collaborator, the man approached his grandmother to ask about the painting's history.

She is said to have told him it had been purchased during World War Two and that it was "Jewish looted art, stolen from Goudstikker. It is unsellable. Don't tell anyone."

The family, which changed their name at the end of the war, have admitted being in possession of the painting but denied knowing its true origin, according to a statement to Dutch media.

After learning of the painting's history, the family member contacted Brand through an intermediary, believing the only way for it to be returned was for the story to be made public.

The family member told Dutch outlet De Telegraaf: "I feel ashamed. The painting should be returned to the heirs of Goudstikker."

In a statement to the same newspaper, his grandmother said: "I received it from my mother.

"Now that you confront me like this, I understand that Goudstikker's heirs want the painting back. I didn't know that."

Upon being informed of the painting's existence, Brand launched his own investigation.

He discovered the painting had a label on the back and the number 92 etched into its frame.

Brand then searched the archives of a 1940 auction where much of Goudstikker's looted collection was sold and discovered an item under the number 92 titled "Portrait of a Young Girl" by Toon Kelder.

Brand believes the painting had been plundered by Hermann Goering, one of the most powerful figures in the Nazi Party, when Goudstikker fled for Britain in 1940.

It was then sold to Seyffardt at auction before being handed down to his descendant, Brand says.

After launching his investigation, Brand contacted the lawyers of Goudstikker's heirs, who he said confirmed the collector had previously owned six paintings by Toon Kelder.

title.en: Somali piracy adds new strain to global shipping and trade routes
title.zh: 索马里海盗活动给全球航运和贸易路线带来新的压力

summary.en: As ships reroute around Africa to avoid Middle East conflict zones, piracy off Somalia is back. The resurgence is driving up insurance, transit times and security costs, putting new pressure on global supply chains.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As ships reroute around Africa to avoid Middle East conflict zones, piracy off Somalia is back. The resurgence is driving up insurance, transit times and security costs, putting new pressure on global supply chains.

It's been a nightmare two months for global shipping , with the Strait of Hormuz largely shut to commercial traffic and the threat of fresh attacks on vessels in the Red Sea.

Even before the latest escalations between the United States , Israel  and Iran , around half the vessels bound for Europe from Asia and the Gulf were bypassing the Red Sea and Suez Canal due to earlier strikes  by the Iran-backed Houthis .

Faced with the threat of attacks around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the narrow chokepoint between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, major shipping firms opted instead for the long detour around southern Africa.

This diversion adds two to three weeks and thousands of nautical miles to the journey, taking ships right past Somalia's coastline — the same waters where Somali pirates staged a multiyear campaign of hijackings that peaked in 2011. Sporadic incidents have been reported ever since.

That stretch of sea is now seeing piracy return with a vengeance, with three ships hijacked off Somalia and nearby Yemen in the past three weeks alone. As of May 8, 2026, the Honour 25 and Eureka oil tankers and the cargo ship Sward all remain under pirate control.

Experts believe that organized crime groups in Somalia are taking advantage of the Iran war to launch hijackings, as international naval patrols, first deployed in 2008 to counter the pirates, have been stretched thin by current events around Hormuz and the Red Sea.

Tim Walker, senior researcher for transnational threats and organized crime at South Africa's Institute for Security Studies, says the pirates now perceive fewer deterrents along Somalia's 3,300-kilometer (2,050-mile) stretch of coastline, which is the longest in all of continental Africa.

"Some groups, organized by ... piracy kingpins, are now looking to seize vessels and hold them for ransom, along with the crew on board — sometimes demanding a high ransom for their safe return," Walker told DW.

The European Union's Operation Atalanta, the naval mission tasked with protecting shipping off Somalia, does maintain a steady presence in the western Indian Ocean, operating alongside the multinational Combined Task Force 151. But it is not an escort force, and is responsible for patrolling vast areas.

title.en: A fight for survival: How the UK soured on PM Keir Starmer and Labour
title.zh: 一场生存之战：英国民众对首相凯尔·斯塔默和工党失去信心

summary.en: Keir Starmer led the UK Labour Party to a landslide victory in 2024, but his leadership is now facing significant challenges and tests.
summary.zh: 凯尔·斯塔默在2024年带领英国工党取得了压倒性胜利，但他的领导力目前正面临严峻的挑战和考验。

body.en:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer's future was thrown into doubt ⁠after his Labour Party ⁠suffered heavy losses in local elections last week. Source: AAP / Maja Smiejkowska/PA

United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who entered office with a confident majority , is now a leader who looks on the ropes, as he fights internal, and external battles.

Less than two years after Starmer led Labour to one of the largest parliamentary majorities in the UK's modern history, his authority is being tested by local election losses , internal rebellion and a public attitude that has hardened against him.

More than 30 Labour MPs have called for him to quit or set out a timetable for his departure, after the party suffered the worst local election defeats for a governing party in more than three decades.

Across 136 English councils, the weekend's electoral test has exposed the scale of Labour's erosion, with Nigel Farage's Reform UK winning more than 1,450 council seats. The right-wing populist party captured former Labour heartlands including Sunderland and Barnsley, key Conservative territories such as Essex and Suffolk, and made major breakthroughs in Scotland and Wales.

At home, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has publicly backed his UK counterpart, telling ABC radio on Monday: "He is a friend of mine, and I hope that Keir Starmer continues to serve as prime minister of the United Kingdom.

"We've dealt with four prime ministers of Great Britain since I was elected as prime minister, and the revolving door of leaders does not lead to stability."

For Starmer, the question is now no longer how to govern from strength — but how to retain power at all.

Labour's 2024 general election victory was initially hailed as an earthquake in British politics.

After 14 years of Conservative rule, voters delivered a decisive repudiation of a government weakened by the enduring fallout of Brexit, Boris Johnson's "partygate" scandal, Liz Truss' market-shaking mini-budget and years of economic stagnation.

Labour secured 411 seats, gaining 209 from its 2019 total — marking its first national victory in 19 years and returning the centre-left party to power for the first time since Tony Blair.

Meanwhile, the Conservatives, also known as the Tories, collapsed to 121 seats, losing 244 in one of the most catastrophic defeats in modern British electoral history.

Starmer campaigned on promises to expand the economy, lower illegal immigration and reduce waiting lists in the National Health Service, presenting Labour as a disciplined corrective to years of Conservative instability.

But for many Britons, the result was less an ideological embrace of Labour than a punitive rejection of Conservative chaos.

reflection.en: Political leadership often involves navigating periods of intense scrutiny, even after significant success. This verse reminds us that ultimate authority rests with God, who determines the rise and fall of leaders and nations. It encourages a perspective that looks beyond immediate political fortunes to the divine hand at work in the world.
reflection.zh: 政治领导力常常需要在取得巨大成功后，依然面对严峻的考验。这节经文提醒我们，最终的权柄在于雅伟，祂决定着领袖和国家的兴衰。它鼓励我们超越眼前的政治浮沉，看到世界背后那双神圣的手。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: Former Thai Prime Minister Thaksin let out of prison early
title.zh: 泰国前总理他信获准提前出狱

summary.en: Thailand's influential former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra has been released from prison early and will wear an electronic monitor during his four-month probation.
summary.zh: 泰国颇具影响力的前总理他信·西那瓦获准提前出狱，在为期四个月的缓刑期间将佩戴电子监控设备。

body.en:
Thailand's influential former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra will be required to wear an electronic monitor during his four-month probation period.

Thailand 's former Prime ‌Minister ⁠Thaksin ⁠Shinawatra was released from prison on parole ‌on Monday.

In September 2025, the Supreme Court had ordered the 76-year-old telecommunications billionaire to serve one year in prison for a past corruption conviction .

Thaksin walked free from Klong Prem Central Prison in Bangkok around 7:40 a.m. local time (00:40 UCT).

He hugged waiting family members and greeted the several hundred supporters wearing the signature red shirts of Thaksin's Pheu Thai party who had gathered outside of the jail.

The corrections department announced Thaksin's parole in April , citing his age and that he had less than a year left to serve as reasons for early release. He will be required to wear an electronic monitor during his four-month probation period.

Thaksin will return to the Shinawatra family home in Thonburi, just south of the capital Bangkok, according to the Thai Examiner.

For two decades, Thaksin has been a key rival of Thailand's pro-military, pro-monarchy elite.

He was first elected as prime minister in 2001 on the back of populist promises of prosperity for the rural poor. Reelected by an overwhelming majority in 2005, he was ousted in a military coup in 2006.

He fled Thailand in 2008 after found guilty of conflict of interest, abuse of power and corruption during his time in office.

Upon his return to Thailand in 2023 , he was sentenced to an eight-year prison term.

But he was only in prison for a few hours before complaining of chest pains and was moved to a hospital. He spent six months there before being freed on parole. The  king later commuted his sentence to one year .

After his daughter Paetongtarn Shinawatra was dismissed as prime minister in August 2025 , a court ruled that Thaksin and his doctors had unnecessarily prolonged his hospital stay. He was ordered to serve the one year in prison for those past convictions.

Although his Pheu Thai Party had its worst ever performance in February 2026 elections, it is part of the governing coalition.

The government is led by PM Anutin Charnvirakul and his conservative Bhumjaithai Party. Unlike Thaksin, Anutin is widely viewed as being strongly supported by Thailand's influential military and royalist elites.  

Thaksin's nephew, Yodchanan Wongsawat, is the minister of higher education in the current cabinet.

His daughter Paetongtarn, Anutin's predecessor, told reporters last week after meeting with Thaksin in prison that they had "not discussed anything about politics" and only spoken about family.
body.zh: 泰国颇具影响力的前总理他信·西那瓦将被要求在四个月的试用期内佩戴电子监视器。 泰国前总理他信西那瓦周一假释出狱。 2025 年 9 月，最高法院下令这位 76 岁的电信亿万富翁因过去的腐败定罪而入狱一年。 他信于当地时间上午 7:40 左右（世界标准时间 00:40）从曼谷 Klong Prem 中央监狱步行获释。 他拥抱了等待的家人，并向聚集在监狱外的数百名穿着他信领导的为泰党标志性红衬衫的支持者致意。 惩教部门于四月宣布他信假释，理由是他信年龄大，而且他信的期限还剩不到一年，以此作为提前释放的理由。在四个月的试用期内，他将被要求佩戴电子监视器。 据《泰国观察报》报道，他信将返回位于首都曼谷以南吞武里的西那瓦家族住宅。 二十年来，他信一直是泰国亲军事、亲王室精英的主要竞争对手。 2001年，他凭借民粹主义对农村贫困人口繁荣的承诺首次当选总理。 2005年，他以压倒性多数再次当选，2006年在军事政变中被赶下台。 2008 年，他因任职期间存在利益冲突、滥用权力和腐败等罪名而逃离泰国。 2023年返回泰国后，他被判处八年监禁。 但他只在监狱里呆了几个小时，就抱怨胸痛并被转移到医院。他在那里待了六个月，然后获得假释。国王后来将刑期减为一年。 2025 年 8 月，他的女儿 Paetongtarn Shinawatra 被解除总理职务后，法院裁定他信和他的医生不必要地延长了他的住院时间。他因过去的罪行被判入狱一年。 尽管他领导的为泰党在 2026 年 2 月的选举中表现最差，但它是执政联盟的一部分。 政府由总理 Anutin Charnvirakul 和他的保守派 Bhumjaithai 党领导。与他信不同的是，阿努丁被广泛认为得到了泰国有影响力的军方和保皇党精英的大力支持。 他信的侄子约查南·旺萨瓦 (Yodchanan Wongsawat) 是现任内阁的高等教育部长。 他的女儿、阿努丁的前任上周在监狱中与他信会面后告诉记者，他们“没有讨论任何有关政治的事情”，只谈论了家庭。

reflection.en: The early release of a powerful former leader, even under monitoring, reminds us of the ongoing tension between justice and mercy in human affairs. Micah 6:8 calls us to consider what is truly required: to do justice, love kindness, and walk humbly. This principle applies to all, from those in power to those administering the law, shaping how societies...
reflection.zh: 一位有影响力的前领导人获准提前出狱，即使受到监控，也提醒我们人类事务中公义与怜悯之间持续存在的张力。弥迦书6:8呼吁我们思考真正需要的是什么：行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心与你的雅伟同行。这一原则适用于所有人，从掌权者到执法者，塑造着社会如何处理问责与怜悯。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Australia's isolation plan 'one of the stronger responses' to hantavirus globally, Butler says
title.zh: 巴特勒称，澳大利亚的隔离计划是全球应对汉坦病毒的“更强有力措施之一”

summary.en: Australians evacuated from the MV Hondius will quarantine for weeks in a pandemic-era facility outside Perth.
summary.zh: 从“洪迪厄斯”号邮轮撤离的澳大利亚人将在珀斯郊区的一个疫情专用设施中进行为期数周的隔离。

body.en:
The first passengers from the cruise ship began disembarking on Sunday morning, local time. Source: Getty / Chris McGrath

Health Minister Mark Butler says Australia's plan to isolate passengers from a hantavirus-hit cruise ship in a containment facility outside Perth for three weeks is among the strictest global responses to the rare virus.

Four Australian citizens, one permanent resident and a New Zealand national are expected to depart Tenerife in the Canary Islands on an Australian government-supported charter flight at around 3am Tuesday AEST.

Medical personnel will be on board the WA-bound flight, which will land at an RAF base near Perth, and passengers will then be taken to the Bullsbrook Centre for National Resilience.

The biosecurity facility was built by the federal government in 2022 — one of three pandemic prevention facilities, which each have over 500 beds.

None of the repatriated passengers is displaying hantavirus symptoms. Three passengers on the MV Hondius have died , while five others evacuated earlier have fallen ill.

Butler was questioned on why the passengers will quarantine for three weeks, when the incubation period for the illness is up to 42 days.

"Obviously, we will be monitoring advice about what should happen beyond those three weeks. There is an incubation period of 42 days potentially for this virus, but that incubation or the risk of transmission obviously drops off after the first few weeks.

Butler said Australia was taking a "precautionary approach" and acknowledged the Australia-bound passengers may be at more risk of contamination than others, because of the long flight to Australia from Tenerife on a small plane.

"I do make no apology for the fact that this is one of the stronger responses you'll see around the world.

"Many other countries are putting in place quarantine orders at a centre like this or at a hospital, only for two or three days rather than three weeks."

The Australians will be the final group of passengers to leave the ship. Passengers cannot disembark until their plane arrives, and Australia’s flight is scheduled to land last.

Other passengers began disembarking on Sunday morning local time, with several countries having sent planes to repatriate their citizens.

Passengers and port workers at Granadilla in Tenerife wore protective gear during the evacuation, including hazmat suits, face masks and respirators.

Spanish citizens were the first to leave the ship before being flown to Madrid and transferred to a military hospital.

Nearly 150 people were on board when the ship — which was on an Antarctic voyage from South America — arrived in the Spanish territory off the coast of north-west Africa, with all passengers and some crew set to be evacuated.

reflection.zh: 实施数周隔离的决定，体现了公共卫生领域审慎的应对方式，旨在预见潜在危险并采取必要的避险措施。在不确定的时期，智慧指引我们采取积极的步骤，以保护我们的社区并防止更广泛的伤害。

title.en: Trump rejects Iran's peace proposal response as more drone attacks hit Gulf region
title.zh: 特朗普拒绝伊朗和平提议，更多无人机袭击海湾地区

summary.en: Former President Trump rejected Iran's response to a peace proposal, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reiterated concerns about Iran's nuclear material amidst ongoing drone attacks in the Gulf region.
summary.zh: 前总统特朗普拒绝了伊朗对和平提议的回应，而以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡重申了对伊朗核材料的担忧，同时海湾地区持续发生无人机袭击。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's peace proposal response via social media. Source: AAP / Jen Golbeck / Sha Dati / Sipa USA

US President Donald Trump branded Iran's terms for ending the Middle East war "totally unacceptable" on Monday, raising the likelihood of renewed conflict after weeks of negotiations.

Iran had responded to the US' latest peace proposal earlier in the day, while warning it would not hold back from retaliating against any new US strikes or permit more foreign warships in the Strait of Hormuz.

Trump himself provided no details on Iran's counterproposal, but in a brief post on his Truth Social platform made clear he was rejecting it.

"I have just read the response from Iran's so-called 'Representatives.' I don't like it — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!" Trump said.

The back and forth came as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — whose forces launched the war on Iran along with the US military on 28 February — insisted the conflict was not over until Iran's enriched uranium was removed and its nuclear facilities dismantled.

But Iran publicly maintained its defiant line, despite the behind-the-scenes diplomacy.

"We will never bow down to the enemy, and if there is talk of dialogue or negotiation, it does not mean surrender or retreat," Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said via X on Monday.

According to state broadcaster IRIB, Iran's response to the US plan, passed to Pakistani mediators, focuses on ending the war "on all fronts, especially Lebanon" — where Israel has kept up its fight with Iran-backed Hezbollah — as well as on "ensuring shipping security".

It offered little in the way of detail, though the US proposal had reportedly focused on extending the truce in the Gulf to allow for talks on a final settlement of the conflict and on Iran's contested nuclear program.

The impasse unnerved global energy markets, with oil prices opening sharply higher Monday. The international benchmark Brent crude jumped 2.69 per cent to US$104.01 ($144) a barrel on July delivery.

Netanyahu said on Monday that Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium must be removed before the US-Israeli war against Iran could be considered finished.

"It's not over, because there's still nuclear material — enriched uranium — that has to be taken out of Iran. There's still enrichment sites that have to be dismantled," Netanyahu told CBS's "60 Minutes".

He added that Trump was on the same page about the enriched uranium, though the president said in a recent interview that the US could remove it "whenever we want," and that it was "very well surveilled" where it is now.

Trump is expected to press President Xi Jinping of China — a major buyer of Iranian oil — on Iran when he visits...
body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普通过社交媒体拒绝了伊朗的和平提议。资料来源：AAP / Jen Golbeck / Sha Dati / Sipa 美国 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一称伊朗结束中东战争的条件“完全不可接受”，这增加了经过数周谈判后重新爆发冲突的可能性。 伊朗当天早些时候对美国最新的和平提议做出了回应，同时警告称，它将毫不犹豫地对美国的任何新的袭击进行报复，也不会允许更多的外国军舰进入霍尔木兹海峡。 特朗普本人没有提供有关伊朗反提案的细节，但在他的“真相社交”平台上发表的简短帖子中明确表示他拒绝该提案。 “我刚刚读到了伊朗所谓‘代表’的回应。我不喜欢这样——完全不能接受！”特朗普说道。 以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡（其军队于2月28日与美军一起对伊朗发动了战争）坚称，在伊朗的浓缩铀被运走并拆除其核设施之前，冲突不会结束。 但尽管有幕后外交，伊朗仍公开维持其挑衅路线。 伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安周一通过X表示：“我们永远不会向敌人低头，如果谈论对话或谈判，并不意味着投降或撤退。” 据伊朗国家广播公司IRIB报道，伊朗对美国计划的回应已转交给巴基斯坦调解人，重点是结束“各条战线，特别是黎巴嫩”的战争——以色列一直在黎巴嫩继续与伊朗支持的真主党作战——以及“确保航运安全”。 尽管据报道美国的提议重点是延长海湾地区的停战协议，以便就冲突的最终解决方案和伊朗有争议的核计划进行谈判，但它没有提供太多细节。 这一僵局令全球能源市场感到不安，周一油价大幅高开。 7 月份交割的国际基准布伦特原油价格上涨 2.69%，至每桶 104.01 美元（144 美元）。 内塔尼亚胡周一表示，在美以对伊朗的战争结束之前，必须清除伊朗的浓缩铀库存。 “事情还没有结束，因为仍然有核材料——浓缩铀——必须从伊朗运出。仍然有浓缩设施需要拆除，”内塔尼亚胡告诉哥伦比亚广播公司的“60分钟”节目。 他补充说，特朗普在浓缩铀问题上的看法是一致的，尽管总统在最近的一次采访中表示，美国可以“只要我们想要”就将其移除，而且它现在所在的位置“受到了很好的监视”。 预计特朗普将在访问伊朗时向中国国家主席习近平（伊朗石油的主要买家）施压。

reflection.en: In a world grappling with persistent conflict and rejected peace efforts, the call to live at peace remains a profound challenge. Romans 12:18 reminds us to pursue peace as much as it depends on us, even when external circumstances make it difficult. This ongoing tension highlights the deep human longing for reconciliation that often feels just out of reach.
reflection.zh: 在一个冲突不断、和平努力屡遭拒绝的世界里，追求和平的呼召依然是一项深刻的挑战。罗马书12:18提醒我们，只要力所能及，就要与众人和睦，即使外部环境使其变得困难。这种持续的紧张局势凸显了人类对和解的深切渴望，而和解却常常遥不可及。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: 'Not another COVID': WHO urges calm ahead of evacuation of hantavirus-hit cruise ship
title.zh: “不要再来一个新冠”：世卫组织敦促保持冷静，准备撤离汉坦病毒感染的邮轮

summary.en: Authorities in the Canary Islands are preparing to evacuate a cruise ship after a hantavirus outbreak killed three passengers.
summary.zh: 加那利群岛当局正准备撤离一艘邮轮，此前船上爆发汉坦病毒，已导致三名乘客死亡。

body.en:
World Health Organization chief Dr Tedros Adhanom said the outbreak was "not another COVID". Source: Getty / Chris McGrath

Countries have prepared to evacuate their citizens from a luxury cruise ship hit by a deadly strain of hantavirus that is due to anchor near the Canary Islands, as health authorities said the risk of the virus spreading was low.

The World Health Organization (WHO) briefed member states with nationals on board on Saturday on how to manage the process , advising active monitoring of passengers for 42 days from the last point of exposure.

"I need you to hear me clearly: this is not another COVID. The current public health risk from hantavirus remains low," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus wrote in a letter to the public published on X earlier.

He said he wanted to take the unusual step of sharing a statement to address people's concerns.

"Passengers will be ferried ashore at the industrial port of Granadilla, far from residential areas, in sealed, guarded vehicles, through a completely cordoned-off corridor, and repatriated directly to their home countries. You will not encounter them," he added.

The luxury cruise ship MV Hondius left for Spain on Wednesday from the coast of Cape Verde off the west coast of Africa after the WHO and European Union asked the country to manage the evacuation of passengers onboard after the hantavirus, which typically begins with flu-like symptoms, was detected.

Usually, the virus is spread by rodents but can in rare cases be transmitted person-to-person.

The WHO on Friday said that eight people had fallen ill, including three who died — a Dutch couple and a German national.

Six of these people are confirmed to have contracted the virus, with another two suspected cases, the WHO has said.

The ship is expected to anchor near the island early Sunday morning, local time.

Local authorities have said the evacuation must take place between midday Sunday midday and around the same time Monday before conditions at sea are expected to become stormier for the rest of the month.

Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, and the Netherlands will send planes to evacuate their citizens aboard the Tenerife-bound cruise ship, Spain's interior minister said in Madrid on Saturday.

The European Union is sending two further planes for the remaining European citizens, Fernando Grande-Marlaska added. The US and UK have confirmed planes and contingency plans were being arranged for non-EU citizens whose countries were unable to send air transport, he said.

British passengers and staff on the cruise ship will be taken to a hospital in northwest England for an initial isolation period once they are repatriated, UK health authorities said on Saturday.

title.en: Trump's China visit set to test fragile truce
title.zh: 特朗普访华将考验脆弱的关税休战协议

summary.en: The first US presidential visit to China in almost 10 years will test a fragile tariff truce.
summary.zh: 近十年来首次美国总统访华，将考验一项脆弱的关税休战协议。

body.en:
Beijing has confirmed that US President Donald Trump will travel to China this week to meet Xi Jinping.

The visit, from 13-15 May, will be the first to China by a US president in nearly a decade - and comes at a pivotal moment for ties between the world's two largest economies.

Executives from some of America's biggest companies - including Boeing, Citigroup and Qualcomm - are expected to travel with Trump, potentially to make deals with Chinese firms. It will also mark a key test in the fragile trade truce between Washington and Beijing.

In April 2025, Trump unveiled sweeping import taxes on countries across the world, friend or foe.

A major effect of that policy was a tit-for-tat trade war between the US and China that saw them hit each other with tariffs that topped 100%. The tariffs were paused after Trump and Xi's last face-to-face meeting in South Korea in October. But threats from both sides have continued.

Trump won the 2016 election vowing to make trade fairer for the US and to bring manufacturing jobs back to the country.

In 2018, he announced tariffs on $250bn (£185bn) of Chinese imports - the moment that many analysts say the trade war started .

The same year, Trump imposed levies on other trading partners - including Mexico, Canada and Europe - which he said were also taking advantage of the US.

The sweeping measures were a shock, especially for China, said policy researcher Ning Leng from Georgetown University.

"It was the first time they dealt with Trump seriously, and they probably did not expect him to go ahead with it," Leng said.

The US was a key importer of Chinese manufactured goods, putting its workers at risk if American buyers turned away due to Trump's tariffs.

The tensions added to existing issues that have weighed on China's economy for years, including sluggish domestic consumption, high unemployment and a prolonged property crisis.

Exports to the US offered a lifeline for Chinese jobs, but with Trump, that was now put at risk.

"It's harder for one country to withstand a trade war with another that it has a trade surplus with," Leng said.

His administration chose not to lift Trump's tariffs on China, sharing a belief that the US needed to keep a lid on its rival's growth in sectors like technology, Leng said.

Biden also introduced restrictions on Chinese firms, including tech giant Huawei, which was essentially ousted from the US over national security concerns. He also put TikTok under scrutiny, with its US operation eventually being separated from its Chinese parent company.

Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) were also effectively blocked from the US market after heavy tariffs were imposed by Biden.

title.en: Europe should behave more like China does if it wants to survive this age of chaos

summary.en: An article suggests that Europe should abandon its traditional rules and adopt a more pragmatic, assertive approach, similar to China's, to navigate the current global chaos. It argues that while the US and Israel may have initiated the conflict in Iran, Europe and China stand to lose the most.
summary.zh: 一篇文章建议，欧洲若想在当前的全球混乱中生存，就应放弃其传统规则，采取一种更务实、更强硬的做法，类似于中国的行事方式。文章认为，尽管美国和以色列可能挑起了伊朗的冲突，但除了交战方本身，欧洲和中国将是损失最大的。

body.en: Instead of obsessing over rules that have ceased to matter, we must consider giving Beijing a dose of its own medicine The US and Israel may have started the war in Iran, but – apart from the belligerents themselves – it is China and Europe that stand to lose the most from it. Yet while European leaders watch like rabbits caught in the headlights as energy prices shoot through the roof, China has responded to the crisis with remarkable equanimity. It is striking how self-confident Beijing is ahead of this week’s Trump-Xi summit. That’s because China is better prepared for what I call an age of “un-order”. This is not the same as disorder, where rules exist but are broken. Un-order is a world where the rules themselves have simply ceased to matter. While European governments have been obsessed with preserving order, China has been working out how to survive chaos. title.en: The geopolitical weaponization of shipping channels
title.zh: 航运渠道的地缘政治武器化

summary.en: The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has renewed focus on other key shipping routes. Experts warn that waterways like the Taiwan Strait or the Strait of Malacca are increasingly used to exert pressure.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The crisis around the Strait of Hormuz has renewed focus on other key shipping routes. Experts warn that waterways like the Taiwan Strait or the Strait of Malacca are increasingly used to exert pressure.

Could imposing a toll to pass through the Strait of Malacca, the narrow stretch of water that connects the Indian Ocean with the Pacific, be a profitable business?

Indonesia's Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa seemed to float the idea at the end of April. "If we split it three ways between Indonesia , Malaysia, and Singapore, that could be quite something, right?" he said.

He later clarified that he was not being entirely serious after Indonesian Foreign Minister Sugiono said that his country supported the freedom of navigation and would not be imposing tolls on vessels passing through the strait, which runs between Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore.

Nonetheless, the remark raised the specter of maritime traffic being misused for geopolitical leverage, not just in the Strait of Hormuz , but in other waterways, too. "The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has forced policymakers in Asia to face questions over the security of other maritime chokepoints," wrote the Reuters news agency.

The Strait of Malacca is of particular concern. This is the most important  shipping route between East Asia, the Middle East, and Europe, accounting for around 22% of international maritime trade.

But there are other issues of concern besides piracy and regional conflict. In November last year, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) warned of this new danger.

Even non-state actors are now in a position to seriously disrupt the flow of global trade, the think tank said, citing attacks by the Houthi militia in the Red Sea. Many shipping companies now avoid passing through the Suez Canal, taking the longer route around the Cape of Good Hope instead, which significantly impacts supply chains and prices.

Political scientist Nikolaus Scholik, former colonel in the Austrian army and senior advisor at the Austria Institute for European and Security Policy (AIES), believes that these are signs of a fundamental change in the geopolitical balance of power .

"We are experiencing today the consequences of a development in which individual states believe they can legally dominate strategically important maritime straits," he told DW. It would be particularly dangerous, he added, if straits like Hormuz, Malacca, or Taiwan were to become levers of geopolitical influence.

summary.en: The US president is reportedly seeking China's assistance to influence Iran and resolve current diplomatic challenges. This reliance on China comes with a potentially significant cost, including implications for Taiwan.
summary.zh: 据报道，美国总统正在寻求中国的帮助，以影响伊朗并解决当前的国际外交困境。这种对中国的依赖可能带来高昂的代价，包括对台湾的影响。

body.en: The US president will be counting on China to influence Iran and help him out of his latest mess. But the price may be high – including for Taiwan Like an out-of-control wrecking ball, swinging wildly back and forth, Donald Trump smashes up the international order without much thought for the consequences. Lacking coherent strategies, workable plans or consistent aims, he power-trips erratically from one fragile region, tense warzone and complex geopolitical situation to another, leaving misery, confusion and rubble in his wake. Typically, he claims a bogus victory, demands that others repair the damage and pick up the tab, then looks around for something new to break. The president will bulldoze into another international minefield this week – the fraught standoff between China and Taiwan – when he travels to Beijing for a two-day summit with President Xi Jinping. After a string of humiliating policy implosions over Ukraine, Gaza, Nato, Greenland, and now Iran and Lebanon, needy Trump craves a diplomatic success to flaunt at home. But his hopes of vote-winning trade pacts are overshadowed by his latest war of choice. He needs Xi’s promise not to arm Iran if all-out fighting resumes – and Xi’s help keeping the strait of Hormuz open as part of a mooted framework peace deal. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国总统将指望中国影响伊朗并帮助他摆脱最近的困境。但代价可能很高——包括台湾。唐纳德·特朗普就像一个失控的破坏球，疯狂地来回摆动，粉碎了国际秩序，没有考虑到后果。由于缺乏连贯的战略、可行的计划或一致的目标，他的权力不稳定地从一个脆弱地区、紧张战区和复杂的地缘政治局势转移到另一个地区，留下痛苦、混乱和瓦砾。通常，他会声称取得了虚假的胜利，要求其他人修复损坏并承担责任，然后四处寻找新的东西来打破。本周，总统将前往北京与国家主席习近平举行为期两天的峰会，届时他将陷入另一个国际雷区——中国与台湾之间的紧张对峙。在乌克兰、加沙、北约、格陵兰岛，以及现在的伊朗和黎巴嫩等问题上一系列令人羞辱的政策崩溃之后，贫困的特朗普渴望在国内取得外交成功。但他赢得选票的贸易协定的希望被他最近选择的战争所掩盖。他需要习近平承诺，如果全面战争重新爆发，不会武装伊朗 — — 并需要习近平帮助保持霍尔木兹海峡开放，作为拟议框架和平协议的一部分。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In moments of complex international diplomacy, leaders face immense pressure to navigate difficult situations where the stakes are high. When a leader finds themselves in a 'mess' and reliant on others, the need for profound wisdom becomes paramount. James 1:5 reminds us that if anyone lacks wisdom, they should ask God, who gives generously, offering...
reflection.zh: 在复杂的国际外交时刻，领导人面临巨大压力，必须驾驭高风险的困境。当一位领导人发现自己陷入“困境”并依赖他人时，对深刻智慧的需求变得至关重要。雅各书1:5提醒我们，如果有人缺乏智慧，就当向神祈求，神必厚赐于众人，不加责备，提供超越人类策略的指引。

verse.textEn: If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.
verse.textZh: 你们中间若有缺少智慧的，应当求那厚赐与众人、也不斥责人的神，主就必赐给他。

title.en: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope?
title.zh: 德黑兰、台湾、贸易……特朗普在中美峰会钢丝上将面临哪些危险？

summary.en: The US leader is set to meet with his Chinese counterpart in Beijing for highly anticipated talks. He enters these discussions from a vulnerable position, hoping to secure economic benefits despite a turbulent global environment.
summary.zh: 美国领导人即将前往北京与中国领导人举行备受期待的会谈。他在一个脆弱的立场上进入这些讨论，希望在全球动荡的背景下取得经济上的胜利。

body.en: US leader enters talks with superpower rival from vulnerable position, but will be hoping for economic wins amid turbulent backdrop If all goes to plan over the next few days – and that is a big if – Donald Trump will arrive in Beijing on Wednesday for a highly anticipated summit with Xi Jinping , China’s leader. The trip will mark the first time a US president has visited China in nearly a decade. The last visit was also made by Trump , during his first term, in 2017. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国领导人处于弱势地位与超级大国竞争对手进行谈判，但希望在动荡的背景下取得经济胜利如果未来几天一切按计划进行 — — 这是一个很大的假设 — — 唐纳德·特朗普将于周三抵达北京，与中国领导人习近平举行备受期待的峰会。此行将是美国总统近十年来首次访华。上次访问也是特朗普在 2017 年第一任期期间进行的。继续阅读...

reflection.en: High-stakes summits between global powers often involve navigating complex challenges and inherent tensions. Romans 12:18 reminds us of the ongoing call to pursue peace, even when circumstances are difficult and outcomes uncertain. It encourages leaders and nations alike to strive for peaceful coexistence, as far as it depends on them.
reflection.zh: 全球大国之间的高峰会晤常常涉及驾驭复杂的挑战和固有的紧张关系。罗马书12:18提醒我们，即使在困难重重、结果不确定的情况下，也要持续追求和平。它鼓励领导人和国家尽其所能，努力实现和平共处。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Hong Kong dissident Nathan Law on China spies in UK: ‘We’re not surprised’
title.zh: 香港异议人士罗冠聪谈中国在英国的间谍活动：“我们不感到惊讶”

summary.en: Nathan Law, an exiled Hong Kong protest leader, expressed no surprise at the conviction of two men for spying in the UK, which raises concerns about access to sensitive information. Law himself lives with a £100,000 bounty from Chinese authorities.
summary.zh: 流亡的香港抗议领袖罗冠聪对两名男子在英国被判间谍罪表示不意外，这引发了对敏感信息获取方式的严重担忧。罗冠聪本人也面临中国当局悬赏的10万英镑。

body.en: Law says conviction of two men for spying raises serious concerns about how they accessed sensitive information Nathan Law, an exiled leader of the Hong Kong student protest who lives with a £100,000 bounty on his head from the Chinese authorities, was not surprised to discover a spy ring had photographed him entering the Oxford Union for an evening debate in November 2023. The conviction at the Old Bailey of Chi Leung “Peter” Wai, 38, and Chung Biu “Bill” Yuen, 65, for assisting a foreign intelligence service, was a sobering first – no Chinese spies had been convicted in British criminal history before Thursday – but the details that came out in the nine-week trial mainly served to confirm his suspicions. Continue reading...
body.zh: 罗表示，两名男子因间谍罪被定罪，引发了人们对他们如何获取敏感信息的严重担忧。香港学生抗议活动的流亡领袖罗冠聪 (Nathan Law) 生活在中国当局悬赏 10 万英镑的悬赏金中。当他发现间谍团伙拍到他在 2023 年 11 月进入牛津大学联盟参加晚间辩论时，他并不感到惊讶。老贝利法院对 38 岁的 Chi Leung “Peter” Wai 和 Chung Biu “Bill” Yuen 进行了定罪， 65 号协助外国情报部门的指控是一个发人深省的第一次——周四之前，英国犯罪史上还没有中国间谍被定罪——但在为期九周的审判中公布的细节主要证实了他的怀疑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of foreign espionage against dissidents reminds us of the vulnerability of those who speak out against powerful regimes. Proverbs 28:15 describes how a wicked ruler can be like a roaring lion or a charging bear over a helpless people, extending their reach to suppress dissent. In such times, we pray for courage for the persecuted and for justice to...
reflection.zh: 针对异议人士的外国间谍活动提醒我们，那些敢于对抗强大政权的人是多么脆弱。箴言28:15描述了邪恶的统治者如何像咆哮的狮子或冲锋的熊一样对待无助的人民，伸出他们的手压制异议。在这样的时刻，我们为受迫害者祈求勇气，并祈求公义得以伸张。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Former China defence ministers convicted of corruption in latest purge of military leaders
title.zh: 中国前国防部长因腐败被定罪，军事领导层最新一轮清洗

summary.en: Two former Chinese defence ministers, Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe, have been sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve after being convicted of bribery. These are among the most severe sentences in a years-long purge of military leaders.
summary.zh: 中国前国防部长李尚福和魏凤和因受贿罪被判处死刑，缓期两年执行。这是多年来对军事领导人进行清洗中最为严厉的判决之一。

body.en: Ex-defence ministers, Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe both sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, among the most severe sentences in a years-long purge Two former Chinese defence ministers were given suspended death sentences for bribery on Thursday, after being convicted by China’s military court, in some of the most severe punishments to be handed down in a years-long purge of the military. Chinese state media Xinhua announced on Thursday that Li Shangfu and Wei Fenghe were both sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, meaning that their sentences will probably be commuted to life imprisonment if Li and Wei demonstrate good behaviour. Continue reading...
body.zh: 前国防部长李尚福和魏凤和双双被判处死刑，缓期两年执行，这是长达一年的整肃行动中最严厉的判决之一。周四，两名前中国国防部长因受贿罪被中国军事法院定罪，被判处死刑缓期执行，这是多年来军队整肃行动中最严厉的一些处罚。中国官方媒体新华社周四宣布，李尚福和魏凤和双双被判处死刑，缓期两年执行，这意味着如果李尚福和魏凤和表现良好，他们的刑期可能会被减为无期徒刑。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The conviction of former defence ministers for bribery highlights the destructive power of greed, which can lead even those in high office to severe consequences. This serves as a sober reminder that the pursuit of wealth above all else often results in profound personal and public grief.
reflection.zh: 前国防部长因受贿被定罪，凸显了贪婪的破坏力，即使身居高位者也可能因此面临严峻后果。这提醒我们，将财富置于一切之上，往往会带来深刻的个人和公共悲痛。

verse.textEn: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
verse.textZh: 贪财是万恶之根。

Chi Leung “Peter” Wai, 38, and Chung Biu Yuen, 65, also known as Bill, were found guilty at the Old Bailey of assisting a foreign intelligence service, making them the first people in British history to be convicted of spying for China. Continue reading...
body.zh: 池良伟和钟标源因在“影子警务”行动中监视异见人士而被定罪 英国边境部队一名官员和驻伦敦的香港贸易官员被判犯有为中国从事间谍活动并通过“影子警务”行动监视异见人士的罪名。 38 岁的 Chi Leung “Peter” Wai 和 65 岁的 Chung Biu Yuen（又名 Bill）在老贝利被判犯有协助外国情报机构罪，这使他们成为英国历史上第一批因为中国从事间谍活动而被定罪的人。继续阅读...

Jeremiah 22:3 reminds those in authority of their divine mandate to act justly, rescue the oppressed, and do no wrong to the vulnerable, including foreigners. This principle underscores the need for...

verse.textEn: Do what is just and right. Rescue from the hand of the oppressor the one who has been robbed.
verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: ‘They have built a machine that pulls out their mother tongue’: why Tibet’s children ‘think they are Chinese’

summary.en: Parents say the insistence on Mandarin in schools is eroding the Tibetan language and culture right from early childhood Weeks after a Tibetan-speaking five-year-old started preschool, she had “completely stopped speaking Tibetan”, according to her mother. Nine months later,...

body.en: Parents say the insistence on Mandarin in schools is eroding the Tibetan language and culture right from early childhood Weeks after a Tibetan-speaking five-year-old started preschool, she had “completely stopped speaking Tibetan”, according to her mother. Nine months later, although the child could still understand Tibetan, she only answered in Mandarin, and at best a few single-word answers in Tibetan after some time. Instead the girl “keeps saying that she can only speak Chinese … that she is Chinese and not Tibetan”, according to a researcher who met the family. “The mother thinks that the daughter is just repeating what she is constantly told at school and that the government aims to eradicate Tibetan.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 家长们表示，学校坚持讲普通话正在侵蚀藏族语言和文化，据她的母亲说，一名说藏语的五岁孩子进入学前班几周后，她就“完全不再说藏语了”。九个月过去了，虽然孩子还能听懂藏语，但她只用普通话回答，一段时间后最多只能用藏语回答几个字。相反，据一位见过这家人的研究人员称，这名女孩“一直说她只会说中文……她是中国人，不是藏人”。 “母亲认为女儿只是在重复她在学校经常被告知的事情，政府的目标是消灭藏人。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to hope, endurance, and faithful rebuilding. Romans 12:12 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with steady hope and perseverance, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到盼望、忍耐与重建。Romans 12:12提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以坚定盼望与忍耐来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: We also glory in our sufferings, because we know that suffering produces perseverance; perseverance, character; and character, hope.
verse.textZh: 就是在患难中也是欢欢喜喜的；因为知道患难生忍耐，忍耐生老练，老练生盼望。

title.en: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai honored by DW
title.zh: 香港亲民主派出版商黎智英获德国之声表彰

summary.en: Hong Kong pro-democracy publisher Jimmy Lai, who founded the city's largest pro-democracy newspaper, has been honored by DW. Lai is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence. His son stated that the award signifies that those who champion the freedom of others are not isolated in their efforts.
summary.zh: 香港亲民主派出版商黎智英被德国之声授予荣誉。黎智英曾创办香港最大的亲民主报纸，目前正在服20年监禁。他的儿子表示，这个奖项表明那些为他人自由而奋斗的人“从不孤单”。

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent nearly 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW has awarded Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award.

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

Sebastien Lai, Jimmy Lai's son and a longtime advocate for his release, told DW that "people who fight for freedom, people who fight for the freedom of others are never alone." And it's meaningful at a time when "a lot of media in Hong Kong now are self-censoring."

"I think if he knew about it [the award], he'd be very happy," Sebastien Lai said.             

DW Director General Barbara Massing said that with the award, DW is honoring Jimmy Lai's "indispensable dedication to democratic values."

"Jimmy Lai has stood unwaveringly for press freedom in Hong Kong at great personal risk, even as space for independent journalism became increasingly limited. With Apple Daily, he gave journalists a platform for free reporting and a...
body.zh: 在入狱20年之前，黎智英创办了香港最大的民主报纸。他的儿子表示，该奖项表明那些为他人自由而奋斗的人“永远不会孤单”。 黎智英 (Jimmy Lai) 12 岁，身无分文，从中国南方偷渡到香港，他只寻求自由和未来。当时，黎智英无法想象他的生活将如何与这个前英国殖民地永远交织在一起。 黎智英在 2020 年 12 月被拘留前几个月接受德国之声采访时表示，“我将与船一起沉没，因为这个地方给了我一切。”黎智英是北京在镇压亲民主抗议活动后对香港实施的“国家安全法”中首批成为目标的知名人士之一。 在2019年反对引渡法案的示威演变成针对北京侵犯香港公民自由的大规模抗议活动后，北京曾表示，该法律将使香港“从混乱中恢复秩序”。 此后，这位亲民主媒体大亨在香港戒备森严的赤柱监狱中被单独监禁近2000天。 黎智英长达数年的审判于今年 2 月结束，78 岁的他因“勾结外国势力”被判处 20 年徒刑。虽然他对所有指控均表示不认罪，但他的法律团队表示他不会上诉。 这一判决是迄今为止根据国家安全法作出的最重处罚，对许多人来说，黎智英的审判象征着香港新闻自由的严重侵蚀，而这是北京压制批评声音的更广泛战略的一部分。 为了表彰他对新闻自由和言论自由的捍卫，德国之声授予黎智英今年的言论自由奖。 自 2015 年以来，德国之声言论自由奖一直向记者和人权捍卫者授予荣誉，以此呼吁人们关注世界各地对新闻自由的限制和人权状况。 黎智英的儿子塞巴斯蒂安·赖（Sebastien Lai）是黎智英释放的长期倡导者，他告诉德国之声，“为自由而战的人，为他人的自由而战的人从来都不是孤独的。”在“香港很多媒体现在都在自我审查”的情况下，这很有意义。 “我想如果他知道这个奖项，他会非常高兴，”塞巴斯蒂安·赖说。 德国之声总干事芭芭拉·马辛表示，德国之声通过这一奖项来表彰黎智英“对民主价值观不可或缺的奉献”。 “黎智英冒着巨大的个人风险，坚定不移地维护香港的新闻自由，尽管独立新闻的空间变得越来越有限。通过《苹果日报》，他为记者提供了一个自由报道的平台和……

reflection.en: The recognition of Jimmy Lai's work, even amidst his imprisonment, reminds us of the cost some pay for standing for truth and freedom. This echoes the biblical promise that those who suffer for righteousness are blessed, finding a profound solidarity and purpose in their trials. Their unwavering commitment, though challenging, points to a hope that...
reflection.zh: 黎智英先生的工作在身陷囹圄之际仍获表彰，这提醒我们，为真理和自由挺身而出需要付出代价。这与圣经的应许相呼应，那些为义受逼迫的人是有福的，他们在苦难中找到深刻的同在和意义。他们坚定不移的承诺，尽管充满挑战，却指向超越当前境况的盼望。

verse.textEn: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
verse.textZh: 为义受逼迫的人有福了，因为天国是他们的。

title.en: Police find body in search for alleged triple murderer Julian Ingram
title.zh: 警方在寻找三重凶手朱利安·英格拉姆时发现尸体

summary.en: The body, believed to be of Julian Ingram, has been discovered by police.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Julian Ingram, who allegedly killed three people in a shooting spree, has been found dead. Source: AAP / Supplied

A body believed to be of an alleged triple murderer has been found in a "very decomposed state" several months after his alleged shooting spree.

Julian Ingram, 37, was accused of killing his pregnant former partner Sophie Quinn, her aunt Nerida Quinn and a third person in the western NSW town of Lake Cargelligo on 22 January.

There had been no positive sightings of Ingram since he was seen driving out of the town in a white getaway ute on the day of the alleged shootings.

But on Monday, NSW Police revealed they had found the body of a 37-year-old next to a white Ford Ranger, alongside a firearm, at Roundhill Nature Reserve, about 100km northeast of Lake Cargelligo.

While he is yet to be formally identified, the vehicle's registration number matched the ute used on the day of the murders.

Police found the council worker's licence inside the car, and the clothing on the body has led officers to believe it is Ingram.

"It's a relief for those involved in the investigation, and probably a bigger relief for the people of Lake Cargelligo and the Quinn family," Western Region commander Andrew Holland told reporters.

"It brings closure to this investigation, it brings closure to the people of Lake Cargelligo and gives some solace to the town, so they can relax."

Ingram was believed to have committed the murders just hours after reporting for bail at a local police station.

Quinn, 25, and her friend John Harris, 32, were killed when bullets were fired into a dark hatchback on Lake Cargelligo's Bokhara St about 4.20pm.

Soon after, her 50-year-old aunt was shot dead at a home on Walker St, a two-minute drive away.

Kaleb Macqueen, 19, was also shot at the home but survived with serious injuries.

The shootings shocked the region, with locals urged to exercise extreme caution as police launched their manhunt.

For weeks, officers scoured the nearby bushland looking for signs of Ingram, eventually expanding their search to the remote outpost of Mount Hope, a former mining town about 90km northwest of Lake Cargelligo.

As leads dried up, police offered a $250,000 award in March for information that could lead to his capture.

Investigators believed Ingram was alive for at least a week after his disappearance.

Officers will continue investigations into how the death occurred and the state of decomposition will be determined by a coroner.

body.zh: 据称在一次枪击事件中杀死三人的朱利安·英格拉姆被发现死亡。资料来源：AAP/提供 据信是一名三重凶手的尸体在他涉嫌枪击事件几个月后被发现，其尸体处于“高度腐烂的状态”。 37 岁的朱利安·英格拉姆 (Julian Ingram) 被指控于 1 月 22 日在新南威尔士州西部小镇卡杰利戈湖 (Lake Cargelligo) 杀害了怀孕的前伴侣索菲·奎恩 (Sophie Quinn)、她的姨妈内里达·奎因 (Nerida Quinn) 和第三人。 自从英格拉姆在据称的枪击事件发生当天开着一辆白色越野车离开小镇以来，就没有任何关于他的正面目击事件。 但周一，新南威尔士州警方透露，他们在卡杰利戈湖东北约 100 公里处的圆山自然保护区发现了一名 37 岁男子的尸体，尸体旁边有一辆白色福特 Ranger，旁边还有一把枪。 虽然他的身份尚未正式确定，但该车辆的车牌号码与谋杀当天使用的皮卡相符。 警方在车内发现了该市议会工作人员的驾照，并且尸体上的衣服使警方相信他就是英格拉姆。 西部地区指挥官安德鲁·霍兰德告诉记者：“这对参与调查的人来说是一种解脱，对卡杰利戈湖的人们和奎因家族来说可能是一种更大的解脱。” “这结束了这次调查，为卡杰利戈湖的人们带来了结束，并给小镇带来了一些安慰，让他们可以放松下来。” 据信英格拉姆在当地警察局申请保释几小时后就犯下了谋杀罪。 下午 4 点 20 分左右，25 岁​​的奎因和她 32 岁的朋友约翰·哈里斯在卡杰利戈湖博卡拉街的一辆黑色掀背车上被子弹射中身亡。 不久之后，她 50 岁的姑妈在两分钟车程外的沃克街 (Walker St) 的一所房子里被枪杀。 19 岁的卡莱布·麦奎恩 (Kaleb Macqueen) 也在家里遭到枪击，但幸免于难，伤势严重。 枪击事件震惊了该地区，警方敦促当地人在搜捕行动时要格外小心。 几个星期以来，警察们在附近的丛林中搜寻英格拉姆的踪迹，最终将搜索范围扩大到霍普山的偏远前哨基地，这是一个前采矿小镇，位于卡杰利戈湖西北约 90 公里处。 由于线索枯竭，警方在 3 月份悬赏 25 万美元，以寻找可能导致他被捕的信息。 调查人员相信英格拉姆失踪后至少还活着一周。 官员将继续调查死亡是如何发生的，尸检情况将由验尸官确定。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: 'Go for government': Western Sydney One Nation's next target after by-election win
